subject: Region pinning + tenant-scope proofing — questions and artifacts
messages:
From: Tom Hayes <t.hayes@stratuspay.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: Olivia Reed <olivia.reed@stratuspay.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Region pinning questions for Dedicated deployment

Soojin — thanks again for the demo last week. StratusPay is evaluating a Dedicated deployment and our security team has asked a few precise items we need confirmed before procurement can proceed. Can you confirm the following for a tenant that's pinned to eu-west-1?

1) Physical/data plane locality: does all customer data (user inputs, model tokens, embeddings, caches) ever leave the pinned region for storage or processing? If there are background replication jobs, where are those copies stored?

2) Control plane metadata: do any identifiers, indexes, telemetry, or audit logs get replicated to Redwood control plane services in another region? If so, what fields are involved and how are they protected/hashed?

3) Backups & snapshots: frequency, storage location, and deletion workflow. Can we require snapshots to be stored only in-region and have a contractual timeline for secure deletion?

4) Deletion attestations: when termination is triggered, what is the step-by-step wipe timeline (from tombstone to physical scrub) and can Redwood provide a signed attestation or report?

5) Logs & retained telemetry: what is default retention for request/trace logs and are they configurable per tenancy? Where are logs archived (and encrypted) and do they contain PII or prompt text by default?

If you can point me to any artifacts (diagram, matrix, or a short runbook) that would be great. We may also want a one-hour deep-dive with your engineering/ops team.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Tom
Tom Hayes
Head of Infrastructure Risk, StratusPay
security@stratuspay.com
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Tom Hayes <t.hayes@stratuspay.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Region pinning questions for Dedicated deployment

Tom — thanks for laying this out clearly. Attached is a short diagram and a tenant-scope matrix that should answer most of the questions; summary below and happy to book a deep-dive.

High level answers (summary):
- Data plane: All customer payloads (prompts, responses, KV cache, embeddings) are served and stored on compute/storage nodes allocated to your Dedicated pool in eu-west-1. By default we do not replicate application data outside the pinned region for Dedicated customers.
- Control plane metadata: Our control plane holds orchestration metadata and non-sensitive routing identifiers. We do replicate minimal metadata (instance IDs, tenant id, health checks) to the control plane located in our managed region (US-EAST-1) to support orchestration and billing. We can provide a reduced-metadata mode where only a hashed tenant id and aggregated health metrics are sent.
- Backups & snapshots: We take periodic snapshots of model cache and persistent stores. For Dedicated deployments we offer an in-region snapshot policy; snapshots can be constrained to eu-west-1 at contract time. Deletion is via a three-step process (tombstone -> secure overwrite -> snapshot purge); typical purge starts at 30 days after termination unless a custom SLA is requested.
- Deletion attestations: We produce a signed wipe certificate and a short forensic timeline on request. For enterprise contracts we can include an attestation appendix in the SOW.
- Logs & telemetry: By default request traces and debug-level logs are retained 90 days; audit logs (auth, admin actions) are retained 365 days. Logs can be configured per-tenant to shorten/extend retention. Request traces may include prompt hashes but not raw prompt text unless debug mode is enabled (debug mode is off by default for Dedicated). All logs at rest are encrypted via customer-managed KMS on Private deployments and via Redwood KMS for hosted Dedicated.

Attachments: geo-isolation-diagram.png, tenant-scope-matrix.xlsx
Next steps: can we schedule a 60-minute session with our Ops engineer and your security lead? I'm available Tue/Wed mornings PT.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Security & Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Tom Hayes <t.hayes@stratuspay.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Region pinning questions for Dedicated deployment

Tom — quick commercial follow-up to Soojin's technical answers. We can add a region-pin clause and the reduced-metadata mode into the Dedicated contract appendix. Typical commercial options we've done for other financial customers:
- In-region snapshot retention (contractual) with a 30/90/180-day purge option.
- Inclusion of a deletion attestation delivered within 10 business days of termination.
- Optional SOC2 bundle upload (if needed we can provide timeboxed access to SOC artefacts under an NDA).

I'll attach the small SLA appendix we usually propose for Dedicated customers so your procurement can review redlines.

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-sla-appendix.pdf

If you want pricing for including a shorter purge window or a reduced-metadata control plane, let me know and I can have a quote returned same-day.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Tom Hayes <t.hayes@stratuspay.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: Olivia Reed <olivia.reed@stratuspay.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 14:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Region pinning questions for Dedicated deployment

Thanks Soojin and Ben — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our compliance checklist:

1) Control plane data: can Redwood provide a precise list of control-plane fields that are replicated (e.g., tenant_id, cluster_id, instance ip, last-active timestamp). We need to verify none of these fields contain prompt text or model outputs.

2) Wipe proof granularity: the attestation should state which namespaces were swept (models, cache, object-store prefixes) and include timestamps. The 10-business-day attestation window sounds good but please confirm the exact contents of that report.

3) Third-party backups: do any third-party backups (cloud provider-managed snapshots) ever copy data to a different geography for cross-region redundancy under your current default? If yes, we will require in-region only for our tenancy.

4) Auditability: does Redwood maintain an immutable audit trail for deletion operations (who initiated, job id, hash of contents before/after)? We need that for our auditors.

If you can send the control-plane field list and a sample attestation PDF (sanitized) that will let us clear the procurement gate. Also agree to a 60-minute deep-dive — our security engineering lead (Olivia Reed) will join. We prefer Thu morning CET.

Kind regards,
Tom
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Tom Hayes <t.hayes@stratuspay.com>
Cc: Olivia Reed <olivia.reed@stratuspay.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Region pinning questions for Dedicated deployment

Tom / Olivia — good questions. Short answers/responses below and I've linked an internal runbook and sample attestation in the shared Drive (link above). We'll also send a sanitized PDF of the attestation prior to the call.

1) Control-plane fields: replicated fields are limited to: tenant_id (hashed option available), cluster_id, node_health_status, orchestration_event_ids, and aggregated metrics (CPU, mem, request counts). No prompt text, no model output, and no PII are replicated. We will provide a CSV extract of the fields for your review.

2) Attestation contents: our attestation template includes: scope of sweep (storage prefixes and object keys), list of scrubbed snapshot IDs, timestamped job ids, and SHA256 hashes of wiped manifest files where applicable. We will include signer details and an ops contact.

3) Third-party backups: default provider-managed snapshots do not copy data cross-region for Dedicated pools unless cross-region replication is explicitly enabled. We will include a contractual clause to disable any automatic cross-region replication for StratusPay's tenancy.

4) Immutable audit trail: yes — deletion jobs create an immutable audit record (append-only) containing initiator, job id, timestamps, and pre/post hashes. Records are accessible under your audit-access agreement.

Proposed next steps:
- I will upload the sanitized attestation sample to the Drive by EOD PT.
- Ben will follow up on the contractual language and provide a pricing note for reduced-metadata mode.
- Schedule deep-dive: Thu 20 May 2027 09:00 CET (we'll send a calendar invite).

If you need this in a formal SOW appendix ahead of the call, we can prepare a short addendum (1–2 pages).

Best,
Soojin Lee
Security & Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
